subject: Acme MAP: POC environment setup dependencies
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acme.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Acme MAP: POC environment setup dependencies

Hi Daniel 1

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and next steps to get the POC environment ready. I attached the latest MAP draft (MAP-draft-v2.pdf) and a simple network diagram. Please review and confirm owners below so we can lock the target dates.

POC milestones (POC target start: 2026-10-25 / target close: 2026-11-08)
- Milestone: VPC peering / connectivity
  - Responsibility: Acme network team (lead) + Redwood infra (Nikhil)
  - Dependencies: VPC peering or PrivateLink, route tables, NAT/egress IPs for allowlist
- Milestone: IP allowlist / firewall rules
  - Responsibility: Acme security (lead) + Redwood (provide egress IPs and ports)
- Milestone: SSO / SAML configuration
  - Responsibility: Acme identity (lead) + Redwood (Vivek to configure SSO metadata)
- Milestone: Secrets & KMS
  - Responsibility: Decision by Acme (customer-managed KMS) vs Redwood-managed secrets; Redwood to provide integration pattern and IAM role

Open asks for Acme:
1) Confirm owners for network/SRE and identity teams (provide contact email for each).
2) Confirm whether you want customer-managed KMS (we can accept an AWS KMS key/grant) or allow Redwood to manage secrets for the POC.
3) Any IP allowlist constraints (static egress IPs, ephemeral NATs, region constraints).

Next steps from Redwood:
- Nikhil will draft the specific egress IP ranges and peering options (VPC peering vs PrivateLink).
- Vivek will send SAML metadata and a short checklist for IdP config.

Attached: MAP-draft-v2.pdf, network-diagram.png

If the owners and answers above look right, we can schedule a short technical kickoff next week (30 min) to align on peering and SSO.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T16:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme MAP: POC environment setup dependencies

Hi Marissa 1

Appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifying Qs from our side so the network team can scope work:
1) For VPC peering, do you require specific CIDR allocations on our side or just route table entries?
2) What are the egress IPs we should allow? Are these static for the POC or subject to change?
3) For SAML, what metadata format do you need (XML metadata file?) and do you support OIDC as well?
4) For KMS, does Redwood need direct access to our key (grant) or do you recommend we provision an IAM role that Redwood assumes?

Network contact: netops@acme.com (I can loop them in once we have a proposed IP list).

Timeline: having peering and allowlists in place by 2026-10-20 would be ideal on our side. Can you confirm if that’s feasible?

Thanks,
Daniel Park
Senior Product Manager, Data Platform | Acme Inc
Daniel.Park@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acme.com>
Date: 2026-10-07T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme MAP: POC environment setup dependencies 1 action items

Nikhil / Vivek 1

Looping you both in to own the infra items from Redwoods side. Per Daniels note, Acmes netops contact is netops@acme.com and theyd like peering + allowlists by 2026-10-20.

Please confirm below ownership and deliverables:
- Nikhil: Own VPC peering options + egress IP list. Deliverable: short doc with two options (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), list of egress IP ranges we can commit to for the POC, and any IAM/test role requirements. Target: 2026-10-09 EOD.
- Vivek: Own SSO/SAML and KMS integration checklist. Deliverable: SAML metadata XML + step-by-step IdP config checklist and recommended KMS pattern for POC. Target: 2026-10-09 EOD.

Daniel 1 once Nikhil and Vivek confirm, well put together a 30-min tech kickoff (tentatively 2026-10-11) to walk through the network diagram and SSO steps.

Marissa

--
Attached: network-diagram.png

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acme.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-08T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme MAP: POC environment setup dependencies 1 infra details

Marissa / Daniel / Vivek 1

Following up with the infra options and what we need from Acme. High-level recommendations: we can support either VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink. For the POC the fastest path is VPC peering if Acme is comfortable with route propagation; PrivateLink is more work but isolates routing.

Key asks from Acme:
- Provide a CIDR range we can peer to (or allow us to propose an allowed CIDR on Redwood side).
- Provide a test IAM role or an account ID for cross-account role setup if you want us to configure customer-managed KMS grants.
- Confirm whether your firewall is stateful (so we can advise on port rules).

Static egress IPs (example ranges we can commit to for POC):
- 3.21.45.80/29
- 3.21.45.88/29
(We will finalize the exact allocation but these are the blocks we expect to NAT from in us-west-2.)

KMS options:
1) Customer-managed KMS: Acme creates a key and grants Redwood the ability to use it via an IAM role/grant. This is the recommended production-like setup.
2) Redwood-managed secrets: Redwood stores secrets in our managed secrets store for the POC; limited lifetime and confined to the POC environment.

I attached the SSO/KMS checklist (sso-reqs.xlsx) 1 Vivek, please add any SAML specifics.
